title: Canonical URL concept (not a guarantee of indexing)
learningObjectives: Explain canonical url concept (not a guarantee of indexing) and choose appropriate document or embedded-resource metadata.

understand.concept: A canonical link element identifies a preferred URL for substantially duplicate or similar pages. It is a hint to search engines, not a guarantee that a particular URL will be indexed or selected. Canonical URLs should be absolute and point to the intended preferred page.
understand.whyItMatters: Incorrect canonical links can consolidate signals to the wrong page. Use them carefully on duplicate variants and keep canonical targets consistent with redirects and sitemap URLs.
understand.analogy: A canonical URL is like marking the preferred copy of a document when several copies contain nearly the same material.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; metadata and embedding behaviour follow browser, HTTP, and search-engine processing rules.

explain.narrative: The link declares a preferred URL for the page. Search engines may consider the hint alongside other signals.

examples.explanation: The link declares a preferred URL for the page. Search engines may consider the hint alongside other signals.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered or document-head example demonstrating the HTML feature.

practise.guidedTask: Identify duplicate URL variants for a sample course page and choose a canonical target. Explain why the tag does not guarantee indexing.
practise.independentTask: Prepare a document head or embed example. Check accessibility, security permissions, and whether metadata accurately describes the content.
hints: Use absolute canonical URLs when declaring a canonical target.
Never treat crawler directives as access control.
Use restrictive iframe permissions and a meaningful title.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Canonical URL concept (not a guarantee of indexing)</title></head><body>
<head><link rel='canonical' href='https://www.example.com/courses/html/forms'></head>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Does a canonical link guarantee that a URL will be indexed?
questions.explanation: Canonical is a hint and does not guarantee indexing or selection.

questions.prompt: Which principle should guide metadata and embedding?
options: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
Use metadata as a substitute for authentication
Grant every embedded document all permissions
questions.answer: Accurate description, least privilege, and no false security assumptions
questions.explanation: Metadata should be accurate and embedded resources should receive only necessary capabilities.
